title: Infrastructure Before Output: How Museum of Toronto Built a Digital Ecosystem by Doing the Wrong Things First
content:
Most conference talks about digital strategy focus on the answer. The ecosystem is in place, the team is aligned, the numbers look good. At a recent MuseumNext event, Davin Henson of Museum of Toronto offered something different: a candid account of the years between having a digital presence and having a digital ecosystem, including the wrong turns, the misleading metrics, and the sequencing principle that finally made the work hold together.

Henson had spoken at MuseumNext in 2021 and 2022 about content strategy and digital distribution. Those were honest talks, he said, but early-stage ones. This time he told the fuller story, structured as three phases and one principle: infrastructure before output, in that order.

title: When Boxing Gloves Meet Museum Walls
content:
There is often a wide gulf between culture lovers and sports enthusiasts. In Antwerp, a hyperdiverse city where martial arts of every kind are widely practised, many practitioners have never set foot in a museum, and plenty of museum regulars have never set foot in a boxing gym. At MuseumNext, three speakers from the city explained how an exhibition is starting to bridge that divide.

Hélène De Pagie, a programme maker at the MAS (Museum aan de Stroom), was joined on stage by Rachid Atia of the Heritage Lab and Jamal Touala of Sporting A, the city’s sports department. Together they told the story of the Martial Arts exhibition, which has brought fighters, wrestlers and boxers into one of Antwerp’s most prestigious cultural spaces, and museum visitors into a world many of them had never given much thought.
